beliefs: f splits input on whitespace runs, reverses each word, and joins with single spaces [E2, E3, E4, E5]
If there is more than one word, 'lmKA' is inserted immediately before the last reversed word with a space before it [E2, E3, E4, E5]
If there is exactly one word, 'lmKA' is prepended to the reversed word [E1, E6]
Leading/trailing whitespace is stripped; whitespace-only or empty input yields just 'lmKA' [E1, E3, E4]
A single word surrounded by whitespace (e.g. ' a ') is treated as one word, so output is 'a lmKA' — lmKA goes after, not before [E6]
notes: Fixed the single-word-with-surrounding-whitespace case: ' a ' and '  ab  ' produce 'a lmKA'/'ba lmKA', so lmKA is appended after the reversed word when the original had leading/trailing whitespace but only one token. Distinguishing this from the no-whitespace single-word case (lmKA prepended) requires tracking whether whitespace was present.
